claims.text: The starting material is an untreated or as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The dual phases in the lamellar microstructure are secondary to the proposed aging treatment rather than being created by it.
A single aging treatment can produce controlled precipitation of secondary phases in the eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Dislocation pile-ups occur near internal boundaries in the untreated lamellar eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries generate local stress concentrations and microcracking during straining.
Controlled secondary-phase precipitation will hinder dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries.
Hindering dislocation pile-ups will reduce local stress concentrations and microcracking.
Reducing local stress concentrations and microcracking will improve tensile ductility.
Aging will improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
Aging will retain or increase tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed effect is applicable at room temperature.
The proposed effect is applicable under standard atmospheric conditions.
The exact magnitudes of the ductility and strength changes are undetermined without experimentation.
Room-temperature tensile testing of aged and untreated specimens can test the hypothesis by comparing tensile strength and tensile ductility.
The hypothesis is falsified if aging produces no significant ductility improvement or decreases tensile strength.
